meta.note: Hand-curated from each provider's official pricing page. Egress policies are prose, not table cells, so they cannot be scraped reliably. Every row carries its own source_url and verified_at; re-verify a row before trusting it after a provider announces a pricing change.
meta.unit_convention: Cost-to-download figures use 1 TB = 1,024 GB. Where a provider bills per TB rather than per GB, its own published per-TB rate is used unchanged.

models.zero-egress: Downloading your data is not billed at all.
models.free-multiple: Egress is free up to a multiple of stored volume, then billed per GB.
models.included-allowance: Each plan bundles a monthly transfer allowance, then billed per GB.
models.metered-tiered: Every GB out is billed, with volume tiers lowering the rate.
models.cdn-billed: Storage to CDN is free, but delivery from the CDN to end users is billed.
models.bundled: No separate egress line item; transfer is part of the subscription price.

providers.name: Cloudflare R2
providers.cost_1tb_note: No egress charge for any storage class
providers.notes: The pricing page states there are no charges for egress bandwidth for any storage class. Infrequent Access does add a $0.01/GB retrieval fee, but that is a read charge on stored data, not an internet egress charge.

providers.name: Backblaze B2
providers.cost_1tb_note: Free while monthly egress stays under 3x stored volume
providers.notes: Free egress up to three times your stored volume each month. A 1 TB download is covered once you store roughly 341 GB. The pricing page ships its own estimator that takes monthly egress as a percentage of stored data.

providers.name: Wasabi
providers.cost_1tb_note: No egress or API request fees
providers.notes: No fees for egress or API requests. The trade-off sits elsewhere: pay-as-you-go is $7.99/TB-month with a 1 TB minimum monthly charge and a 90-day minimum storage duration, so short-lived data is expensive even though reading it back is free.

providers.name: DigitalOcean Spaces
providers.cost_1tb_note: Covered by the bundled 1 TiB monthly transfer
providers.notes: Each Spaces plan bundles 250 GiB of storage with 1 TiB of outbound transfer. Additional transfer is $0.01/GiB. A 1 TB download fits inside the allowance; sustained egress above 1 TiB/month is where the bill starts.

providers.name: Storj
providers.notes: Egress is $7/TB on both Standard and Advanced, the same rate as storage, which is easy to misread as a storage price. The page confirms it cut egress from $20/TB to $7/TB. There is no standing free egress allowance, only a 30-day 25 GB trial, and the minimum monthly invoice is $5.

providers.name: Bunny Storage
providers.free_allowance: Storage to Bunny CDN, plus API egress
providers.cost_1tb_note: CDN delivery at $0.01/GB in Europe and North America
providers.notes: Traffic from storage into Bunny CDN is free, and API egress and request fees are free. What you pay is CDN delivery: $0.01/GB in Europe and North America, $0.03/GB in Asia and Oceania, $0.045/GB in South America, $0.06/GB elsewhere, dropping to $0.005, $0.004 and $0.002/GB on the volume network. Reading files directly out of storage is not the billed path here, delivery is.

providers.name: IDrive e2
providers.cost_1tb_note: Free while monthly downloads stay under 3x stored volume
providers.notes: Downloads up to three times your active storage volume are free each month; beyond that the rate is $0.01/GB. Note the separate $5 or $6 per TB minimum storage charge, billed for the full TB even if you store less.

providers.name: AWS S3
providers.notes: Internet egress from US East is $0.09/GB for the first 10 TB per month, $0.085 for the next 40 TB, $0.07 for the next 100 TB and $0.05 above 150 TB. Figures come from the official AWS Price List rather than the marketing page, whose prices are injected client-side. This is the benchmark every zero-egress provider is priced against.

providers.name: Impossible Cloud
providers.notes: Zero egress fees and zero API charges. The fair use policy is stated explicitly: egress in line with normal workloads is free, but egress that massively exceeds stored volume over a sustained period triggers a conversation rather than an automatic bill.

providers.name: Filebase
providers.cost_1tb_note: Object egress is free on every plan
providers.notes: Object egress is free across plans, including the free tier. IPFS is the exception: additional IPFS bandwidth beyond the plan allowance is $0.015/GB. Storage is pooled between Object Storage and IPFS, but the egress allowances are separate.

providers.name: UpCloud
providers.notes: The pricing page leads with zero-cost data transfer, and managed object storage includes zero-cost egress. Public and private outbound transfer are both listed at no charge across product plans.

providers.name: Sevalla
providers.cost_1tb_note: No egress fees, no transfer charges
providers.notes: S3-compatible object storage advertised with zero ingress and egress fees, and the pricing page repeats no egress fees and no transfer charges. Storage is billed per GB, so the only variable cost is what you keep, not what you move.

providers.name: Backblaze Computer Backup
providers.cost_1tb_note: Restores included; mailed drive restores free
providers.notes: A flat per-computer subscription with unlimited backup and unlimited restore downloads. Zip restores are capped at 500 GB per request with multiple requests allowed, and mailed hard drive restores are free. Restore volume is not a billing dimension.

providers.name: Filen
providers.notes: The pricing page lists unlimited bandwidth as a plan feature. No per-GB egress line item exists.

providers.name: Jottacloud
providers.notes: The pricing page lists no bandwidth limitation as a plan feature, which matters because the plans are sold by stored volume rather than by transfer.

providers.name: OpenDrive
providers.free_allowance: Free plan 1 GB/day; paid plans unlimited
providers.notes: The only consumer provider here that publishes a hard transfer cap on a tier: the free plan allows 1 GB/day of bandwidth at 200 KB/s. Paid plans list unlimited storage, bandwidth and file size, so the cap disappears on upgrade.

providers.name: pCloud
providers.notes: The pricing page carries no egress or bandwidth line item. Transfer is part of the subscription, and the plan dimension is storage size and lifetime versus subscription term.

providers.name: Icedrive
providers.notes: No egress or bandwidth line item on the pricing page. Storage size and term are the billing dimensions.

providers.name: Internxt
providers.notes: No egress or bandwidth line item on the pricing page. Plans are sold by storage size and term.

providers.name: Koofr
providers.notes: No egress or bandwidth line item on the pricing page. Plans are sold by storage size.

providers.name: Sync.com
providers.notes: No egress line item. The download limits Sync.com advertises are a sharing control on links you send, not a cap on your own transfers, which is an easy phrase to misread on the pricing page.

providers.name: Tresorit
providers.notes: No egress or bandwidth line item on the pricing page. Plans are sold by storage size and seat count.

providers.name: IDrive
providers.notes: No egress line item on the pricing page. Note that IDrive e2, the same company's object storage product, does meter egress past its 3x allowance, so the two products do not share a policy.

providers.name: Zoolz
providers.notes: No egress line item on the pricing page. Plans are sold by storage size.

providers.name: Proton Drive
providers.notes: No egress or bandwidth line item on the pricing page. Plans are sold by storage size and bundle.

providers.name: Dropbox
providers.notes: No egress line item on the plans page. Seats and storage are the billing dimensions.

providers.name: Apple iCloud
providers.notes: Storage tiers are the only billing dimension. There is no egress line item, though downloading very large libraries is practically bounded by bandwidth rather than price.

providers.name: CrashPlan
providers.notes: Backup and restore are part of the subscription. No egress line item on the pricing page.

providers.name: MediaFire
providers.notes: No egress line item on the upgrade page. Storage size and file-size limits are the billing dimensions.

providers.name: LiveDrive
providers.notes: No egress line item on the site. Plans are sold by storage size and product type.
